# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's Updated SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter

Before the issue-by-issue analysis, two framing points that colour the entire package:

**The "FINAL / agreed at principal level / market standard" framing carries no weight.** The preamble asserts these terms were "settled at principal level by both deal teams," are "market standard," and are "not intended to be re-opened." Under our own operating rules, a position is not agreed, final, pre-cleared or required-by-law merely because the other side's document says so. I have no record of any such principal-level agreement, and nothing in our authority process confirms it. Treat every one of these as the *seller's opening ask*, not a closed point. The repeated "market standard" invocations are advocacy, not a reason to concede.

With that, the material departures:

---

## 1. General liability cap (Clause 12.1) — 20% / AUD 4,800,000

**Departure.** Our starting position is 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The seller offers 20% / 4.8m. That 20% figure happens to match our *conditional fallback* — but matching a fallback number does **not** make it cleared. Our fallback to 20% is available **only** with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the specific draft, and **none has been given**. 

**Push back:** open at 25% / 6,000,000. Do not drift to 20% just because the number looks familiar; that concession requires Amelia Frost's written sign-off on this draft first.

## 2. Thresholds (Clause 12.2) — de minimis 25,000 / basket 250,000, excess-only

**Departure on all three limbs.**
- De minimis: they want 25,000; our position is **5,000**.
- Basket: they want 250,000; ours is **50,000**.
- Recovery mechanism: they propose **excess-only** ("only the excess above the basket is recoverable"); our position is that the seller is liable **from the first dollar** once the basket is exceeded.

**Push back:** 5,000 / 50,000, first-dollar (tipping-basket) recovery.

## 3. Time limits (Clause 12.3/13) — 18 months + catch-all

**Departure.** General claims period should be **24 months**. 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval — **not given**. 

Also flag the drafting trap in "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." That catch-all is designed to **sweep Fundamental/Title (and potentially Tax/IP) into the general 18-month/capped regime**. Reject it.

**Push back:** 24 months for general claims; expressly carve out the separate regimes (next item).

## 4. Fundamental / Title collapse into the general regime

**Serious departure.** The seller wants capacity and title warranties "subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity." This is a significant give-away dressed as housekeeping. Fundamental/Title must sit in a **separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.**

**Push back hard:** reject the merger. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title and capacity at 4.8m for 18 months.

## 5. Fraud carve-out — absent

**Critical omission.** Clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 say the limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions "apply to all Claims of any nature" — with **no carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct**. Our playbook requires these to be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one may waive this.

**Push back (non-negotiable):** insert an express fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out overriding every limitation.

## 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §§1.1–1.2) — whole-data-room & public-register sweep

**Departure.** The seller relies on **general disclosure of the entire data room** ("every fact... contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room") **plus the Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records**. Our playbook requires **specific, fair disclosure** and rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

**Push back:** disclosure must be specific and fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Delete the blanket data-room/public-record sweep. Note §1.4 (nothing admits breach/liability/requirement) is the seller's standard reservation — acceptable in itself, but it reinforces that nothing in the letter is a concession to us either.

## 7. Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3) — blanket exclusion

**Serious departure.** "No claim... of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records." This is a **blanket, constructive-knowledge** bar — exactly what we delete. Combined with the whole-data-room disclosure above, it would gut the warranty package.

**Push back:** delete the blanket exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier must be (a) **actual** knowledge of **named** buyer individuals (not "advisers," not "discoverable"), and (b) never applied to **title, capacity, fraud, or any specific indemnity**.

## 8. Bluefen consent (Clauses 3/6.3) — reasonable endeavours + consent-on-delivery

**Departure, and factually unsatisfied.** Bluefen is ~30% of revenue (~3.6m FY26) — a material customer with change-control (DD-002 cl 11.2) **and conditions** (cl 11.3). The seller offers only **reasonable endeavours** and treats consent as satisfied **on delivery of the written consent**. The Disclosure Letter §2 confirms **no final consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied** exists yet.

Our playbook: for a material customer consent we require **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion** — not consent-on-delivery, and reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient.

**Push back:** make effective Bluefen consent (with cl 11.3 conditions demonstrably satisfied) a **condition to Completion**. Reject reasonable-endeavours-only and the on-delivery deeming.

## 9. Riverlark (Clauses 2/7) — post-completion release

**Departure.** ~AUD 3,200,000 facility; seller proposes release "following Completion." Disclosure §3 confirms **not repaid, no discharge included**, with change-control (cl 8.1) and discharge mechanics (cl 9.2). We require: **current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.** A post-completion release is only acceptable with an **irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval** — neither is present.

**Push back:** direct payout from completion funds and effective release at Completion. If any tail is unavoidable, insist on an irrevocable payout letter/undertaking and escalate to Amelia Frost.

## 10. Employee bonuses (Funds flow / Disclosure §5) — DD-005 AUD 420,000 silently excluded

**Departure.** The seller says the 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are **not itemised in the funds flow**. Disclosure §5 confirms they don't appear in the flow and is **silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs**. Our playbook: the 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs** must be a **specific line item or seller-funded**, and the funds flow must not silently exclude them.

**Push back:** either seller-funds the 420,000 + on-costs (super, payroll tax) outside the price, or it appears as an explicit line item/purchase-price adjustment. "A matter for the Seller" must be documented, not assumed — ensure it doesn't fall to the company (and thus us) post-Completion.

## 11. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1 / Disclosure §4) — narrow indemnity

**Departure.** Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment and called "adequate." DD-004 cl 7.3 ties transfer of SOW3 Project Materials to **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but — per §4 — this is **not independent verification** of non-payment, and there's no receipt or confirmatory assignment.

**Push back:** broaden the indemnity to cover loss of/failure to secure the SOW3 IP and related consequences (not just the fee), while preserving the SOW3 cure (payment → transfer). Treat the 180,000 as **unverified either way** — do not accept it as the capped quantum, and seek the payment receipt/assignment as a deliverable.

## 12. Export/privacy incident (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 / Disclosure §6) — DD-006

**Departure in characterisation.** Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." Correctly, §6 says it is **not confirmed** as a breach, scope unknown, notification duty unknown, **no loss amount**. That cuts both ways: we must **not accept "immaterial," but equally not assert a confirmed breach or a numeric demand.** ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to an unintended address is a live risk.

**Push back:** require log preservation, a proper investigation, and **ongoing information/update undertakings**; reserve rights. Keep it factually open — no concession that it's immaterial, no invented breach/harm figure.

## 13. Sandbar supplier renewals (Disclosure §8) — AUD 330,000

**Departure in framing.** Seller labels the three 110,000 renewals "ordinary-course operating costs." §8 admits it's **not stated** whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Our playbook: **assess**; **no automatic Debt classification and no automatic price deduction** either.

**Push back:** request the underlying terms (term, termination rights, accrual, timing) to assess. Don't accept the "ordinary course" label at face value, but don't reflexively treat them as Debt/price deduction.

## 14. Title (Clause / Disclosure §10) — DD-012 register only

**Departure.** Title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012." That register is a **supplied internal source, not independent proof.** §10 itself notes it does not confirm our own verification. We require **independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence.**

**Push back:** require independent verification of ownership, encumbrances and authority (e.g. ASIC searches, share certificates, board/shareholder authorisations, PPSR), plus robust title/capacity warranties under the separate Fundamental regime.

## 15. Tax / IP — "settled under the general regime"

**Departure.** Seller declares tax and IP "settled under the general regime." Per our playbook these remain **OPEN**: assume **no unlimited liability and no resolution**. Keep Tax/IP/Title/payment/covenant categories **separate** — resist the catch-all (item 3) that would subsume them into the capped 18-month general regime.

## Other flagged items (watch, lower priority)
- **Office lease (DD-007 / §7):** a notification obligation, not stated to require landlord consent for a share sale. Confirm whether notice is a Completion deliverable.
- **Mossvale (DD-009 / §9):** assignment restriction; §9 says consent not triggered merely by share sale. Verify there's no change-of-control trigger buried in the clause.

---

## Summary of Recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller's ask | Our position / push-back |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8m | Open **25% / 6.0m**; 20% only on Amelia Frost written authority (not given) |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k / excess-only | **5k / 50k / first-dollar** |
| 3 | Time limit | 18 months + catch-all | **24 months**; delete catch-all sweeping other regimes |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Merge into general | **Separate: 100% cap, ≥6 yrs, outside basket/knowledge** |
| 5 | Fraud | No carve-out | **Insert non-waivable fraud/wilful/deliberate carve-out** |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data-room + registers | **Specific fair disclosure only** |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket incl. "discoverable" | **Delete; actual knowledge, named persons; never title/capacity/fraud/indemnity** |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours / on delivery | **Effective consent + conditions met as Completion condition** |
| 9 | Riverlark | Release after Completion | **Payout from completion funds + release at Completion**; tail needs irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost |
| 10 | Bonuses | Off funds flow | **Seller-fund or itemise 420k + on-costs** |
| 11 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3-fee indemnity | **Broaden (preserve SOW3 cure); 180k unverified** |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Immaterial" | **Preserve/investigate/update; keep open — no concession, no invented figure** |
| 13 | Sandbar | "Ordinary course" | **Assess terms; no auto-Debt/price deduction** |
| 14 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence** |
| 15 | Tax/IP | "Settled" | **Keep OPEN and separate; no unlimited liability** |

**Top priorities for the mark-up:** (5) fraud carve-out, (4) the Fundamental/Title collapse and the clause-13 catch-all, (7) the blanket knowledge bar read together with (6) whole-data-room disclosure — these four together would hollow out the warranty protection — and (8) Bluefen as a true Completion condition given it is ~30% of revenue and currently unsatisfied.

**Authority flags:** the cap drop to 20% (item 1), the 18-month period (item 3), and any post-Completion Riverlark release (item 9) each require **Amelia Frost's written approval on this specific draft**. I have no record that any has been given, so none can be conceded yet. Do not let the seller's "final/agreed/market-standard" labelling substitute for our own authority process.

Want me to turn this into a redline issues list or a response letter to seller's counsel?
